refutations.argument: The revised stipulation declares that in a game won by one player 'every other player counts as a loser' of it. But a free-for-all game can use the limited range of influence option (806.2a), and under 801.16 a mandatory loop makes the game a draw for each player involved, those players leave the game, and all remaining players continue; one remaining player can then win. In that game the looping player did not lose: the CR says the game is a draw for that player. C3 nevertheless turns that player into a loser, and, as the first to leave, into the first loser who chooses who goes first. 103.1 gives a drawer the draw sentence (the player who made the choice in the previous game chooses), not the loser clause. The carve-out 'if the previous game was a draw' covers only the whole game, so the stipulation overrides an official per-player outcome (a draw) that the CR settles, in a free-for-all game the case's applies_when covers and does not exclude.

source.excerpt: the game is a draw for each player who controls an object

steps.conclusion: In a free-for-all game using limited range of influence, a looping player's game is a draw for that player, who leaves, while the remaining players play on and one of them can win; that player drew and did not lose.

source.excerpt: If the previous game was a draw, the player who made the choice in that game makes the choice in this game.

steps.conclusion: The CR treats a drawn outcome by the draw sentence of 103.1, but C3 counts that drawing player as a loser (and as first loser), so the proposed rule contradicts the official outcome of the game for that player.
